AFWD.justification: The forward transformation mapping pairs of elements to their sum

AREV.justification: The inverse operation identifying which summands produced a specific result

CLINK.justification: The sequential application of set-theoretic constructions to build A from S

ENGAGR.justification: Points that simultaneously act as limits for sum-free sequences and potential sum-collisions

EVALF.justification: The state where the sum of two elements falls back into the forbidden set

EVALT.justification: The state where no two elements in the set add up to a third element in the same set

FFUSE.justification: The recombination of partitioned elements into the unified set A

FSPLIT.justification: The division of the real line into the sum-free set S and its complement

IFIX.justification: The irreversible size constraint fixed by the power of the continuum

IMSCRIB.justification: The preservation of the underlying real number topology during set selection

TANCH.justification: The final Minkowski sum which contains the entire operational output within the target space

VINIT.justification: The state prior to the selection of the real number field or its subsets

phase_3.both_description: The superposition of a set being both a subset and a superset during construction
phase_3.false_description: The condition where x + y is in S, violating the sum-free property
phase_3.true_description: The condition where x + y is not in S for all x, y in S
phase_3.void_description: The null set before any elements are assigned to S or A

steps.domain_action: Initialize the real number field R
Identify the topological properties of R
Partition R into potential sum-free candidates
Select elements for S such that S is sum-free
Fix the sum-free property as a permanent constraint on S
Map S to the power set to prepare for continuum construction
Construct set A with cardinality 2^aleph_0 using elements from S
Branch into individual summands for Minkowski addition
Verify element a1 is in A
Verify element a2 is in A
Recombine all sums into the set A+A
Validate that A+A remains within the real space RS
Seal the set A+A as the terminal mathematical object
